desc:
The string words holds lowercase words separated by single commas. Inside one word every letter is different. Only the set of letters of a word matters, not their order.

Two words are connected if the letter set of one can be turned into the letter set of the other by exactly one of these operations:

  • adding exactly one letter,
  • deleting exactly one letter,
  • replacing exactly one letter by any letter (including the same letter, so two words with equal letter sets are connected).

A group consists of words linked by chains of connected words (two words are in the same group if there is a chain of connections between them). Return [g, m] where g is the number of groups and m is the size (number of words) of the largest group.

"a,b,ab,cde"  -> [2, 3]   (a~b by replacement, a~ab and b~ab by adding a letter; cde is alone)
"ab,ba,abc"   -> [1, 3]   (ab and ba have the same set; abc adds a letter)
"ab,cd"       -> [2, 1]   (turning ab into cd needs two replacements)
constraints: 1 ≤ word length ≤ 26, all letters inside a word are distinct
Words consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Represent each word by a 26-bit mask of its letters. Which masks are connected to a given mask?
Adding or deleting a letter flips one bit, so mask m and m ^ (1 << b) are connected. How can you find the replacement neighbours without trying 26 × 26 masks?

Two masks related by a replacement become equal after you delete one bit from each. For every mask and every set bit, record the 'wildcard' mask with that bit removed and union all words that produce the same wildcard mask.
editorial: Convert each word to a bitmask and use union-find over the words. Words with equal masks are connected directly. Add/delete connections: for every mask m and each set bit b, if m ^ (1 << b) is the mask of some word, union the two words.

A replacement changes mask m into m' by removing one bit and adding another; so m and m' both reduce to the same mask after removing one suitable bit each. For every mask and every set bit store the reduced mask in a dictionary (as a wildcard key, separate from real masks) and union all words that share a wildcard key. This needs only O(26) operations per word instead of O(26²), for O(26 · n) in total.
After all unions, count the roots and the size of the largest set. Comparing all pairs would be O(n²) and also works for small inputs, but the wildcard trick is what makes the problem scale.
